answer: The group repeatedly rejected making rdfs:label a sub- or super-property of P1_is_identified_by. Martin Doerr's original 2018 proposal (thread t1123, 'Issue: Solution for Dualism of E41 Appellation and rdfs:label') was to give P1 two ranges (E41 and rdf:Literal) and declare it a superproperty of rdfs:label so a single query for P1 would also return rdfs:label values. Robert Sanderson objected that this is 'punning' -- letting the same property range over both literals and resources -- which is bad RDF practice; he later (2021, thread t1495, 'RDFS, XML and more') gave the formal reason: rdfs:label is inherently a DataProperty and P1_is_identified_by an ObjectProperty, and OWL2 requires these be disjoint, so a sub/superproperty link between them is actually invalid in OWL DL. Even under plain RDFS entailment it produces nonsense: because P1's range is E41_Appellation, a subproperty assertion forces literal objects of rdfs:label to also be typed E41_Appellation (and E1_CRM_Entity, E90_Symbolic_Object, etc.), which cannot be serialized since literals cannot be subjects/typed resources. Richard Light additionally warned in 2018 that declaring P1 a superproperty of the shared, widely-used rdfs:label would contaminate unrelated RDF data in the same store (any rdfs:label anywhere would suddenly entail P1/E41 assertions), and that the differently-shaped graphs (a full P1->E41 node path vs. a bare literal) still could not be retrieved by one SPARQL pattern regardless of the sub/superproperty declaration -- so it bought nothing technically while adding risk. Mark Fichtner, George Bruseker and Nicola Carboni also pushed back, preferring E41 as a real resource. Instead of tying rdfs:label into the CRM property hierarchy, the group moved in two steps: (1) in the 2018 thread, Martin Doerr and Richard Light worked out a dedicated new CRM property for the literal content itself -- 'has symbolic content' (domain E90 Symbolic Object, range E62 String), a subproperty of rdf:value rather than of/over rdfs:label -- which became P190_has_symbolic_content, letting an E41 Appellation carry its string form without conflating the identification property with a generic RDFS label. (2) In 2021, when the same rdfs:label/P1 equivalence question resurfaced for the published RDFS file, Robert Sanderson (with Thomas Francart confirming the formal mechanism) proposed replacing the direct subPropertyOf assertion with an OWL2 property-chain axiom: 'rdfs:label owl:propertyChainAxiom (crm:P1_is_identified_by, crm:P190_has_symbolic_content)', i.e. inferring 'x P1_is_identified_by z; z a E41_Appellation; z P190_has_symbolic_content y' from 'x rdfs:label y' rather than asserting rdfs:label is itself a sub/superproperty of P1. This gives the desired inferential link between the label shortcut and the full CRM path without declaring type-incompatible properties equivalent.
